name: Moon
description: The Moon is Earht's only natural satellite and is the fifth largest moon in the solar system. It has a significant impact on Earth, influencing tides and stabilizing the planet's axial tilt.

name: Phobos
description: Phobos is the larger and closer of Mars' two moons. It is heavily cratered and is gradually spiraling inward towards Mars, which will eventually lead to its destruction or collision with the planet.

name: Deimos
description: Deimos is the smaller and more distant of Mars' two moons. It has a smoother surface than Phobos and is also slowly moving away from Mars over time.

name: Europa
description: Europa is one of Jupiter's largest moons and is believed to have a subsurface ocean beneath its icy crust, making it a prime candidate in the search for extraterrestrial life.

name: Ganymede
description: Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system and is even larger than the planet Mercury. It has a magnetic field and is believed to have a subsurface ocean, making it another intriguing target for astrobiological studies.

name: Callisto
description: Callisto is the second-largest moon of Jupiter and is heavily cratered, indicating that it has an ancient surface. It is also believed to have a subsurface ocean, although it is less likely to harbor life compared to Europa and Ganymede.

name: Titan
description: Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the second-largest moon in the solar system. It has a thick atmosphere and is known for its lakes of liquid methane and ethane on its surface.

name: Enceladus
description: Enceladus is a small moon of Saturn that has gained significant attention due to its geysers that spew water vapor and ice particles from its subsurface ocean, making it a key target for astrobiological research.
